leopard-s-kopje.name: Leopard's Kopje
leopard-s-kopje.summary: An archaeological site in Zimbabwe that is the type-site for the culture marking the region's Middle Iron Age, known through its classified pottery phases.

bambandyanalo.name: Bambandyanalo
bambandyanalo.summary: An archaeological site in South Africa near the Limpopo River, also called K2, that flourished from the 11th to 13th centuries as a trading hub and predecessor to the Kingdom of Mapungubwe.

lydenburg-heads.name: Lydenburg heads
lydenburg-heads.summary: Seven hollow terracotta heads found with pottery at Lydenburg, South Africa, radiocarbon-dated to about AD 500, among the earliest known African Iron Age artworks south of the equator.

lydenburg.name: Lydenburg
lydenburg.summary: A town in Mpumalanga, South Africa, also called Mashishing, with a history dating back to around AD 500; today a hub for fly-fishing, farming and tourism.

great-zimbabwe.name: Great Zimbabwe
great-zimbabwe.summary: A city in south-eastern Zimbabwe settled around 1000 AD, capital of the Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe from the 13th century and the largest stone structure in precolonial Southern Africa, built by ancestors of the Shona people.

toutswemogala-hill.name: Toutswemogala Hill
toutswemogala-hill.summary: Iron Age settlement in eastern Botswana occupied from the 7th to the late 19th century, part of the formation of early Southern African states built on cattle-keeping.

upemba-depression.name: Upemba Depression
upemba-depression.summary: A large marshy basin in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with about fifty lakes, populated since the 5th century AD and considered the origin of the Kingdom of Luba.

kingdom-of-mapungubwe.name: Kingdom of Mapungubwe
kingdom-of-mapungubwe.summary: An ancient southern African state at the Shashe-Limpopo confluence, with a capital of 5,000 people by 1250, that traded gold and ivory via the Indian Ocean before declining around 1300.

chibuene.name: Chibuene
chibuene.summary: A Mozambican coastal trading site active from the late first millennium AD, linked to Indian Ocean trade networks and later to gold trade with Great Zimbabwe.

indian-ocean-trade.name: Indian Ocean trade network
indian-ocean-trade.summary: A long-distance maritime trade system linking Southeast Asia, South Asia, the Middle East, Africa and the eastern Mediterranean since antiquity, sometimes called the cradle of global trade.

ingombe-ilede.name: Ingombe Ilede
ingombe-ilede.summary: An archaeological site in Zambia near the Zambezi River, a major 16th-century trading centre for salt, copper, gold, ivory and slaves linked to Indian Ocean trade goods.

bosutswe.name: Bosutswe
bosutswe.summary: An archaeological site on a hill at the edge of the Kalahari Desert in Botswana, occupied for around 1,000 years from about 700 AD and known for advanced metalworking from around 1300 AD.

shashe-river.name: Shashe River
shashe-river.summary: A major tributary of the Limpopo River, rising in Botswana and flowing to the point where Botswana, Zimbabwe and South Africa meet.

limpopo-river.name: Limpopo River
limpopo-river.summary: A roughly 1,750 km river rising in South Africa and flowing through Mozambique to the Indian Ocean, first sighted by Europeans when Vasco da Gama anchored off its mouth in 1498.

unguja-ukuu.name: Unguja Ukuu
unguja-ukuu.summary: Historic Swahili settlement on Zanzibar Island, Tanzania.

tumbe.name: Tumbe
tumbe.summary: An early medieval Swahili site on Pemba Island that served as a major Indian Ocean trading hub between 600 and 1000 AD, known for its distinctive pottery.

pemba-island.name: Pemba Island
pemba-island.summary: A Tanzanian island in the Zanzibar Archipelago, on the Swahili Coast of the Indian Ocean.

kongo-people.name: Kongo people
kongo-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group and speakers of Kikongo who lived along the Atlantic coast in the kingdoms of Kongo, Loango and Kakongo, and were among the first Africans to meet Portuguese traders in 1483.

kingdom-of-kongo.name: Kingdom of Kongo
kingdom-of-kongo.summary: A Central African kingdom spanning parts of modern Angola, Congo and Gabon, independent from around 1390 to 1862, later a Portuguese vassal until its monarchy was abolished in 1914.

kingdom-of-loango.name: Kingdom of Loango
kingdom-of-loango.summary: A Kongo-founded state on Africa's Atlantic coast from roughly the 1500s to 1800s, exporting copper and cloth, at its height reaching from Cape St Catherine near the Congo River's mouth.

kakongo.name: Kakongo
kakongo.summary: A small kingdom on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa, a vassal of the Kingdom of Kongo, that became an important commercial center from the 17th through 19th centuries.

shona-people.name: Shona people
shona-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group native to Southern Africa forming the majority in Zimbabwe, who migrated from the Congo River basin around the end of the first millennium and built a great civilization there.

rozvi-empire.name: Rozvi Empire
rozvi-empire.summary: A Shona state on the Zimbabwean Plateau (c. 1683–1866) established by Changamire Dombo, whose name reflects a legacy as a warrior nation; it became the most powerful fighting force in Zimbabwe.

venda-people.name: Venda people
venda-people.summary: A Bantu people native to Southern Africa, closely associated with the 13th-century Kingdom of Mapungubwe, from which their language and traditions are believed to descend.

thomas-huffman.name: Thomas Huffman
thomas-huffman.summary: An archaeologist (1944–2022) who specialized in pre-colonial farming societies in southern Africa and identified the Central Cattle Pattern at Mapungubwe, linking it to the rise of Great Zimbabwe.
